metadata.title: stopHostScreenUpdate() Dead Code — Polling Continues After Logout

sources: NavigationService constructor (line 66) — starts setInterval unconditionally on service instantiation
transformations: setNotConnected() — clears session tokens but does NOT call stopHostScreenUpdate()
!isConnected() check returns true (not connected) → early return
sinks: CPU/event loop: ~1-2ms per callback wasted every 5 seconds after logout
No network requests, no data access, no side effects after !isConnected() guard

privilege_boundary.achieved_privilege: Same — no escalation possible from resource waste

impact.description: Trivial resource waste: one function call every 5 seconds after logout. The !isConnected() guard prevents any API calls or data access. No security escalation possible. VULN-020 fix incomplete — stop method defined but never wired into logout path.

prerequisites: User must authenticate and then logout
Browser tab must remain open after logout

compensating_controls: !isConnected() guard prevents API calls or data access after logout

remediation.fix_approach: Call stopHostScreenUpdate() in StorageService.setNotConnected(). Also add to AppComponent.ngOnDestroy() as defense-in-depth. Consider lazy-starting the polling interval on login rather than in constructor.

history.note: stopHostScreenUpdate() defined but never called (VULN-020 incomplete); polling continues after logout

Confirmed dead code — stopHostScreenUpdate() has zero call sites. !isConnected() guard prevents actual API calls post-logout. Low severity: trivial resource waste, no security escalation. Trivial 1-line fix in setNotConnected().
